newsitem.title: USA: NYS Silver confident budget can be agreed Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: NYS Silver confident budget can be agreed Tuesday.

text.p: The New York State Assembly Speaker said Tuesday he was convinced a budget for fiscal 1998, which was due on April 1, could be agreed to shortly, although optimism a pact would be approved last weekend proved unfounded.

"I'm confident that we can still get it done today," Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, told reporters in Albany, after meeting with his counterpart in the Senate, Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, and Governor George Pataki.

Bruno did not predict that the budget would be agreed to on Tuesday, noting New York State's top three lawmakers still were discussing changes to the state's welfare system. "We made a lot of progress. Last night, this morning, we're really down to a couple of issues that just have to get resolved."

Silver, whose Democrat-led Assembly wants a less restrictive welfare program than the Republican governor, denied any of the budget negotiators had retreated on the issue. "I don't think anybody backed off on anybody."

And Bruno said that the new federal budget pact had not interfered with the state's talks. Explaining New York State was looking at its financial situation, he said, "So that's not impacting us in any negative way, keeping us from coming to a conclusion." He added there were some difficulties in the talks, which he did not disclose.

While Pataki opposes the Assembly's plan to pay workfare participants the minimum wage, or if higher, the prevailing wage, the new federal budget plan would require such workers to be paid the minimum wage.
New York State's budget negotiators were due to resume their talks at around 1330 EDT.
